name: Palmieri ESWT
question: Does focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy improve symptoms or penile deformity compared with sham treatment in Peyronie's disease?

arms.label: sham treatment with a nonfunctioning transducer

design.population: 100 men with Peyronie's disease of no more than 12 months' duration and no prior Peyronie's-related treatment.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Design, setting, and participants; Intervention

verdictNote: Symptom scores improved at 12 weeks; treated plaque size and curvature did not.
takeaway: In a sham-controlled trial, four weekly focused shock wave sessions were followed by improved mean pain, IIEF-5 and quality-of-life scores in the treated arm at 12 weeks, with unchanged plaque size and curvature. At 24 weeks, mean pain scores were below baseline in both arms.

reports.label: Randomized trial
reports.citation: Palmieri A, Imbimbo C, Longo N, et al. "A First Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial Evaluating Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for the Treatment of Peyronie's Disease." *Eur Urol.* 2009;56(2):363-370. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2009.05.012
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Design, setting, and participants

results.measure: Mean visual analog scale (0-10) score at 12 and 24 weeks

values.exp: Significantly improved at 12 weeks; significantly lower than baseline at 24 weeks
values.ctl: Significantly lower than baseline at 24 weeks

results.note: The abstract gives no arm-level means, between-arm effect estimate or prespecified primary endpoint.
